abstract: INTRODUCTION: Persistent lymphatic drainage following retroperitoneal lymph node dissection for testicular tumor is an uncommon complication. CASE PRESENTATION: We describe a 21-year old man of Caucasian origin who had metastatic non-seminomatous germ cell tumor of the testis, and underwent retroperitoneal lymph node dissection, nephrectomy and partial inferior vena cava excision for a residual mass. The patient subsequently developed persistent lymphatic drainage causing foot drop that eventually responded to conservative medical and surgical measures. CONCLUSION: This postoperative condition usually responds well to conservative measures but has the potential for serious morbidity if it is not managed appropriately.
abstract_ja: はじめに：後腹膜リンパ節郭清後の持続性リンパ漏は、精巣腫瘍に対する手術でまれな合併症である。症例提示：転移性精巣非セミノーマ性胚細胞腫瘍の21歳白人男性が、残存腫瘤に対して後腹膜リンパ節郭清、腎摘除、下大静脈の部分切除を受けた。術後に持続性リンパ漏を生じ、足下垂をきたした。最終的には保存的な内科的・外科的処置に反応した。結論：この術後合併症は通常は保存的治療で良好に反応するが、適切に管理しなければ重大な罹患に至る可能性がある。
